newsitem.title: USA: Republicans say they agree with Clinton on goals.
newsitem.headline: Republicans say they agree with Clinton on goals.

text.p: Republican congressional leaders said on Tuesday they had a very positive meeting with Democratic President Bill Clinton and agreed to work on five or six specific goals including a balanced budget by 2002.

"It was a very positive meeting ... We agreed to work on specific goals and specific projects," House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich said after a Capitol Hill meeting between Clinton and bipartisan congressional leaders.

Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, said Clinton and the congressional leaders had agreed to work jointly on five specific areas. They were efforts to move people from welfare rolls into jobs, review of Clinton's education reform proposals, improving juvenile justice, helping the financially floundering city of Washington, and meetings between Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and the chairmen of congressional tax-writing committees to seek agreement on tax cuts.
Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said he would add a sixth area of accord, saying, "we agreed all of this would have to be considered in the overal context of a balanced budget by 2002."

Clinton proposed a plan for balancing the budget by then and for about two decades thereafter in the fiscal 1998 budget he sent to Congress last week. Lott and other Republicans expressed deep misgivings about his plan but agreed it offered a basis for negotiations, unlike budgets that led to political gridlock in the past.

After Tuesday's meeting, Lott said, "Clearly there are some areas where there are substiantial disagreements," such as campaign finance reform. But he and Gingrich emphasised the new atmosphere of conciliation. "We're trying to find a way to take the minimum number of potshots at each other and get on with our work," Lott said.
